title: Balanced arithmetic bound
statement:
Let $c_{\mathrm{in}},c_{\mathrm{out}},m,n$ be natural numbers. If $3^{c_{\mathrm{in}}}\le 2^{c_{\mathrm{in}}}m^2$, $3^{c_{\mathrm{out}}}\le 2^{c_{\mathrm{out}}}(n-m)^2$, $3m\le 2n$, and $3(n-m)\le 2n$, where $n-m$ denotes natural-number subtraction, then
\[
3^{2+\max(c_{\mathrm{in}},c_{\mathrm{out}})}\le 2^{2+\max(c_{\mathrm{in}},c_{\mathrm{out}})}n^2.
\]
replaced:
Let $c_{\mathrm{in}}, c_{\mathrm{out}}, m, n \in \bbn$ satisfy the two inductive bounds
$3^{c_{\mathrm{in}}} \le 2^{c_{\mathrm{in}}} m^2$ and
$3^{c_{\mathrm{out}}} \le 2^{c_{\mathrm{out}}} (n - m)^2$, together with the balance
conditions $3m \le 2n$ and $3(n - m) \le 2n$. Then, writing
$c = 2 + \max(c_{\mathrm{in}}, c_{\mathrm{out}})$,
\[
  3^{c} \;\le\; 2^{c} \cdot n^2 .
\]
